source_quote: I took notes on the whole plan, the way I always do. Not on paper. In my head.

subject: Asha's belief vs knowledge distinction
fact: Asha says 'I believe' about the origin of the spore illness, undermining her authority by revealing uncertainty.
source_quote: I believe.

subject: Asha's contempt for the narrator

source_quote: My dear boy," she said, and then looked at me with contempt, and then turned to Daz. "Tell the Dragonborn that...

subject: Asha's emotional vulnerability

source_quote: I agree!" she said, with a warmth she'd shown none of us since we'd met her. "Like, you would think that in the midst of the abyss with the demons, everyone could get over their relationship issues, but no, no, no, no, no...

subject: Asha’s Final Intelligence Delivery
fact: Asha delivers the true nature of the spore illness — it originates only from Ilvara’s spores — but undermines it with 'I believe,' revealing her uncertainty and transforming authoritative knowledge into fragile opinion.
source_quote: The particular spore illness only originates from Ilvara's spores and from her mushroom. I believe.

subject: Asha’s Revelation of Personal History
fact: Asha reveals she and Jorlan are the only two not captured by Ilvara’s spores — she because she clings to Lolth, he because he hates Ilvara — and discloses their romantic past, exposing vulnerability beneath her contempt.
source_quote: The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan... I mean, they used to have an affair, it used to be this whole thing, and then she broke up with him...

subject: Asha's Test
fact: Asha Vandree conducted a verbal and psychological test on Daz and the party, using theological accusations and emotional pressure to assess their conviction, knowledge, and willingness to act. Her questions were designed to provoke panic or reveal ignorance. The party’s calm, strategic responses — particularly Daz’s use of doubt as sincerity — passed the test, convincing her they are viable agents for her agenda.
source_quote: Well put, well put. This was just a test.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree admitted she was not going to kill Ilvara herself and needed Daz to do it.
source_quote: I was not going to kill her. That is what you… where you come in.

subject: Asha Vandree

source_quote: have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree expresses genuine exasperation and emotional vulnerability about being stuck between Jorlan and Ilvara’s past relationship.
source_quote: Do you have any idea how aggravating that is?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree identifies the spore servants as former drow who embraced Ilvara’s power and the ecstasy of the spores.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... who embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree questioned whether Daz was a wizard who prays to Lolth.
source_quote: You're a wizard. A wizard… a wizard who prays to Lolth?

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree realized Daz was testing her discernment as a follower of Lolth.
source_quote: you are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree reluctantly engages with the party, showing visible effort to speak to them.
source_quote: I could hear the slight effort it cost her to engage with us at all.

subject: Asha Vandree

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree told Daz not to touch her.

subject: Battle of the Heart Fungus
fact: The Battle of the Heart Fungus is a coordinated assault in which the party uses terrain, psychological manipulation, and precise spellcasting to dismantle Ilvara’s power structure. The Heart Fungus is targeted with the Dust of Suleiman, Ilvara is grappled into Phantasmal Killer by Zalthir, the Glyph of Warding is triggered by Jorlan’s rage, and Thorin engages in melee while Daz and others provide area denial.
source_quote: The glyph went down on the bridge... One 4th-level slot. I'd made my choice. The Dust of Suleiman on the fungus, because Asha was right.

subject: capture status of drow
fact: Only Asha and Jorlan are no longer captured by Ilvara's spores — Asha due to devotion to Lolth, Jorlan due to hatred of Ilvara.
source_quote: The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan... Me, because I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth... and Jorlan, because apparently he really hates Ilvara for something or other.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz claimed he was speaking through the body that had communed with Lolth.
source_quote: I am… you are not speaking to the wizard of this body. I… he… this body has communed with Lolth. And I… I am speaking through this body.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is perceived by Asha as the owner of an ooze familiar, which elevates his status in her eyes.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Daz

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the one who inscribes the Glyph of Warding on the bridge, knowing it will kill anyone crossing it — including Jorlan — without discrimination.
source_quote: I finished the inscription and straightened up. The bridge was now a threshold. Everything on the far side of it was already committed to a detonation it didn't know about yet.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz noticed the small wet sound of Glabbagool opening his eyes and tracking left and right.
source_quote: I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes, which then began tracking left and right with the particular energy of someone who absolutely cannot help himself.

subject: Daz

subject: Daz
fact: Daz said the conviction he shows is the kind this follower of Lolth shows.
source_quote: It's the kind of conviction this follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Daz

subject: Daz

subject: Glyph Detonation
fact: Jorlan’s charge triggers the Glyph of Warding, dealing 21 damage, destroying one spore servant, weakening another, and destabilizing the Heart Fungus. This shifts the tactical balance of the battle.
source_quote: He comes straight onto the bridge, straight onto the glyph, and the detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing...

subject: Glyph detonation trigger
fact: Jorlan is deliberately provoked into stepping onto the Glyph of Warding, triggering its detonation and eliminating one spore servant while damaging the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot!" ... "Jorlan charges. He comes straight onto the bridge, straight onto the glyph, and the detonation is immediate and total...

subject: Glyph Inscription and Trigger Selection
fact: The narrator inscribes the glyph and chooses Jorlan’s side as the trigger zone, not because Jorlan is evil, but because he is not trusted. This decision reflects a pragmatic moral failure — the party kills based on alliance, not justice. The glyph becomes a monument to their compromise.
source_quote: Okay," I said. "And then, I guess the trigger is — anyone approaching from the side that Jorlan is on.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum carefully inscribed the Glyph of Warding into the stone of the bridge, anticipating its use against Jorlan.
source_quote: the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum explained he had Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, and Phantasmal Killer, but only one 4th-level spell slot.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: Grygum

source_quote: Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum laid out his three 4th-level spells as keys for one lock.
source_quote: Three keys. One lock. The planning was, in a sense, just a very elaborate way of deciding which door we most needed to open.

subject: Grygum's Heart Fungus damage
fact: Grygum delivers twenty force damage per turn to the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: delivers twenty force damage per turn

fact: The mushroom icon smolders.
source_quote: the icon smolders.

subject: Introduction of Glabbagool as a Familiar
fact: The party fabricates a cover story that Glabbagool is Daz’s familiar to avoid suspicion. Asha’s shift from alarm to respect demonstrates how status and perception override reality in their world — an ooze is more acceptable if labeled as a familiar.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Jorlan

subject: relationship history between Jorlan and Ilvara
fact: Jorlan and Ilvara had a romantic affair that ended with her breaking up with him, leaving him bitter and emotionally entangled.
source_quote: They used to have an affair, it used to be this whole thing, and then she broke up with him, and then he was bitter because she broke up with him.

subject: Spell Slot Dilemma
fact: Grygum possesses three 4th-level spells but only one spell slot, forcing a strategic decision: which spell to cast — Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, or Phantasmal Killer — and which to sacrifice. The choice will determine whether the team employs infrastructure destruction, psychological warfare, or environmental trapping.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: spell slot limit

subject: Spore Cloud Release
fact: The Heart Fungus unleashes a lethal cloud of spores that forces Zalthir to ascend ten feet to breathe, demonstrating its active hostility and tactical awareness.
source_quote: ...it unleashes a cloud of spores that hits Zalthir so hard he has to climb ten feet straight up just to breathe.

subject: spore infection risk
fact: Spores from Ilvara's fungal network can transform drow into mindless servants, as evidenced by Daz's condition.
source_quote: I mean, — look at him! He's already infected. I don't want to be infected.

subject: spore servant origin
fact: The spore servants are former drow who embraced Ilvara’s claims and succumbed to her spores.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Tactical Reassessment of the Assassination Plan
fact: Grygum’s original plan to target Ilvara directly was overruled after Asha Vandree’s intervention, shifting focus to the Heart Fungus as the primary objective. This reorientation transforms the use of Dust of Suleiman from a direct attack into infrastructure demolition, and redefines the entire mission’s strategy.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus was the key. That was her point, and she wasn't wrong.

subject: The Battle of the Heart Fungus
fact: The battle begins with Zalthir teleporting to grapple Ilvara, the Heart Fungus unleashing spores, spore servants rising, Jorlan triggering the glyph, Thorin engaging in melee, and the Dust of Suleiman detonating on the fungus — all coordinated around Asha’s insight that infrastructure must be destroyed before the person.
source_quote: The final shape of it. Zalthir teleports in, grapples, drops her into the sphere of damage. The Dust of Suleiman burns the Heart Fungus. Daz fireballs the overlap. Thorin holds the line with my crossbow and whatever else he has.

subject: The Glyph Inscription
fact: The glyph was inscribed with the intent to kill anyone approaching from Jorlan’s side — a flawed but workable solution that reflects the party’s moral compromise: they chose to kill Jorlan if he came near, not because he was evil, but because he was a liability.
source_quote: And then, I guess the trigger is — anyone approaching from the side that Jorlan is on.

subject: The Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding detonates on Jorlan, killing one spore servant and severely damaging another and the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: the detonation is immediate and total — 21 damage, one spore servant gone to nothing, another barely holding itself together, and the Heart Fungus itself shuddering from the force of it.

subject: The Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding is inscribed on the bridge to detonate on anyone approaching from Jorlan’s side, regardless of their alignment or motives.
source_quote: The glyph waits on the bridge for whoever tries to reinforce her.

subject: The Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus emits a deadly spore cloud when threatened, targeting Zalthir and others.
source_quote: It unleashes a cloud of spores that hits Zalthir so hard he has to climb ten feet straight up just to breathe.

subject: The Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is the central mechanism of Ilvara’s power, and its destruction dismantles her control over the area.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus was the key. That was her point, and she wasn't wrong. The fungus was how Ilvara kept control over the whole area.

subject: The Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus shudders from the force of the Glyph of Warding’s detonation on Jorlan.
source_quote: the Heart Fungus itself shuddering from the force of it.

subject: The Negotiation with Asha
fact: A high-stakes psychological confrontation in which Daz’s illusion of divine possession is not exposed but reinterpreted by Asha as a divine test — which she believes she has passed. The event reveals Asha’s paranoia as a weapon that bends deception into belief, and exposes her desperation to eliminate Ilvara.
source_quote: She had not seen through the deception. She had reframed it entirely — had taken my con and reclassified it as a *divine test of her discernment*, which she believed she had now passed.

subject: the performance of the Spider Queen
fact: The wizard enacted a multi-layered illusion involving a spider, luminescent lights shaped into the Spider Queen, and a possessed vocal tone — all designed to simulate divine communion with Lolth — which succeeded in appearing authentic but triggered unintended interpretations.
source_quote: "The spider scurried back... I was already weaving the lights around it... The luminescence built. Condensed. The shape of the Spider Queen herself... seemed to pass directly into mine. Then: darkness. The performance was seamless."

subject: The Planning of Ilvara's Assassination
fact: The party consolidates their strategy using Grygum’s three 4th-level spells, weighing the risks of area damage, psychological terror, and silent traps. The decision of which spell to cast becomes the linchpin of the entire mission, forcing tactical prioritization under extreme constraints.
source_quote: Three keys. One lock. The planning was, in a sense, just a very elaborate way of deciding which door we most needed to open.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker acknowledges Asha’s tactical insight about the Heart Fungus being more important than Ilvara’s personal destruction, and chooses to use the Dust of Suleiman on the fungus.
source_quote: I took notes on the whole plan, the way I always do... The Dust of Suleiman on the fungus, because Asha was right and the infrastructure was more important than the satisfying image of Ilvara's nightmares eating her alive.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker acknowledges that the plan is flawed, but workable — and that survival depends on execution, not perfection.
source_quote: A workable one. Jorlan was not our ally, even if he hated Ilvara. We'd made our choice between the two of them, and the glyph would reflect it.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker chooses to target the Heart Fungus over Ilvara’s personal destruction, accepting Asha’s insight as correct.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman on the fungus, because Asha was right and the infrastructure was more important than the satisfying image of Ilvara's nightmares eating her alive.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker chooses to target the Heart Fungus with the Dust of Suleiman, accepting Asha’s insight over personal satisfaction.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman on the fungus, because Asha was right and the infrastructure was more important than the satisfying image of Ilvara's nightmares eating her alive.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker hands Thorin their light crossbow, recognizing his need to contribute meaningfully despite his lack of ranged capability.
source_quote: I can lend you my light crossbow. It's a small thing. But everyone needs a way to contribute when it starts.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker notes that they chose Asha over Jorlan, and the glyph reflects that choice, even though Jorlan hates Ilvara.
source_quote: We'd made our choice between the two of them, and the glyph would reflect it.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker notes the final plan in their mind, not on paper — every spell, every role, every consequence accounted for.
source_quote: I took notes on the whole plan, the way I always do. Not on paper. In my head. Every piece placed, every spell accounted for.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker recognizes the moral ambiguity of the glyph — it kills without discrimination, and they cannot inscribe one that only kills drow they dislike.
source_quote: I don't know how to inscribe a glyph that will only kill the drow that we don't like.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker reflects on Ilvara’s possible nightmares and considers using Phantasmal Killer, but ultimately defers to the more strategic plan.
source_quote: What does she dream about? What would an illusory manifestation of her deepest fears look like?

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker reflects on the moral cost of the glyph — it kills without discrimination, and they cannot design one that only kills enemies.
source_quote: I don't know how to inscribe a glyph that will only kill the drow that we don't like.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin accepts a light crossbow from the speaker, acknowledging his lack of ranged capability and choosing to contribute despite his limitations.
source_quote: So someone lends me a crossbow, and I take it, because I'd rather be in the fight badly than out of it entirely.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin engages Jorlan in melee combat after the glyph detonates, landing a 14-damage hit and applying Sap to gain advantage.
source_quote: The first hit lands true. Fourteen damage, and I roll through the Sap, put him off-balance, give him disadvantage on whatever's coming back at me.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin recognizes Jorlan’s predictable rage and uses it to trigger the Glyph of Warding, turning his emotional state into tactical leverage.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin swings wide with Dawnbringer, rolling a natural 2, and fails to land a second hit on Jorlan despite his staggered state.
source_quote: The second swing goes wide... I'm rolling a 2 and there's nothing in the world that fixes a 2.

source_quote: you're not gonna get within 20 feet of her

source_quote: the town of Sloopdopblop is just eight days away

subject: Zalthir

subject: Zalthir

subject: Zalthir

subject: Zalthir

source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them...

subject: Zalthir
