source_quote: Asha's opening had been a pointed thing — "Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? Convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?" — the kind of question designed to see what shape your panic takes.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir noticed Asha Vandree treated him as furniture during the conversation.
source_quote: She filed me away and returned her eyes to Daz. Not a glance afterward. Not a word in my direction for the duration of the conversation.

subject: Zalthir's teleport-grapple tactic
fact: Zalthir plans to teleport to Ilvara, grapple her, and drop her into the Phantasmal Killer spell to damage both her and the Heart Fungus simultaneously.
source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them, and then the rest of you can fireball or whatever from there.

subject: drow society
fact: Drow society employs deliberate silence as a weapon of erasure and control — a social tactic recognized by Zalthir as deeply painful and psychologically isolating.
source_quote: "There is a particular kind of silence that drow society uses as a weapon... the silence of deliberate erasure. Of being present in a room and being treated as furniture."

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a sentient, controlling organism that reanimates fallen guards as spore servants, emits lethal spore clouds, and serves as the central mechanism of Ilvara’s power. It treats intruders as threats and adapts its tactics dynamically.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus has been sitting in the middle of the cavern this whole time, pulsing, and I have been treating it as terrain. That's a mistake I revise immediately when it unleashes a cloud of spores...

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara is a former high priestess of Lolth who has become seduced by the idea that Lolth wishes to be married to Zuggtmoy, leading her to spread fungal corruption and transform followers into mindless fungal creatures. Her cult is a dangerous, expanding network of infected individuals and corrupted magic.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara’s cult is a heretical offshoot of Lolth-worship that believes the Spider Queen wishes to be married, and has spread fungal corruption through spore-infused allies who have become mindless fungal creatures. The cult’s influence is perceived as a contagious theological and biological abomination by Asha Vandree and others in the cavern.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Ilvara's Cult
fact: Ilvara’s cult is a splinter movement among drow that worships her as a manifestation of Lolth’s will, spreading spores that induce ecstatic submission. Followers are not monsters but former drow who willingly embraced the spores, becoming hollowed-out servants. The cult’s influence is real, seductive, and deadly.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Ilvara's Spore Cult
fact: Ilvara's Spore Cult consists of drow who embraced her claim that she is Lolth’s further manifestation, willingly ingested her spores, and now exist as hollowed-out, ecstatic spore servants — former allies turned into walking consequences of their own surrender.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Lolth's Church (Orthodox)
fact: The orthodox worship of Lolth, as represented by Asha Vandree, views Ilvara’s marriage cult as a blasphemous corruption of divine will. Followers believe Lolth’s power is absolute, untouchable, and not subject to mortal metaphors like marriage. Deviation from this doctrine is seen as infection — both spiritual and biological — requiring eradication.
source_quote: That is not the kind of conviction a follower of Lolth shows.

subject: Lolth's Faithful
fact: Lolth's Faithful, represented by Asha Vandree, reject Ilvara’s heresy as blasphemy. They maintain strict adherence to traditional drow worship of the Spider Queen, viewing the spore cult as a corruption of divine order — and themselves as the only true survivors of ideological purity.
source_quote: I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth, and have rejected all of these claims of the bride heresy.

subject: Lolth’s Faithful
fact: Lolth’s faithful, represented by Asha, reject Ilvara as a heretical false prophet. Devotion to Lolth is framed as a moral and spiritual bulwark against spore corruption, though Asha’s personal credibility is weakened by emotional instability and uncertainty in her claims.
source_quote: I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth, and have rejected all of these claims of the bride heresy.

subject: Lolth's True Followers
fact: Asha Vandree and her kind represent a purist faction of Lolth worship that rejects fungal corruption and views Ilvara’s devotion as heretical blasphemy. Their faith is rooted in rigid dogma, fear of contamination, and a belief that Lolth’s will must be enforced through violence.
source_quote: That is not the kind of conviction a follower of Lolth shows.

subject: The Cult of the Heart Fungus
fact: An underground operation led by Ilvara, the high priestess, centered on the Heart Fungus as both a source of power and a vector of control over the cavern. The fungus sustains Ilvara’s dominance and is the linchpin of her influence, making its destruction the key to dismantling her regime.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus itself wasn't the vector. The spores were Ilvara's. The artifact was the other risk.

subject: bridge as threshold
fact: The bridge, after the glyph inscription, becomes a lethal threshold that detonates against anyone approaching from Jorlan’s side.
source_quote: The bridge was now a threshold. Everything on the far side of it was already committed to a detonation it didn't know about yet.

subject: Bridge of Warding
fact: The bridge is the threshold between the party and Ilvara — inscribed with a glyph, crossed by Jorlan, and the site of the first decisive tactical blow — it is both physical and moral terrain.
source_quote: The bridge was now a threshold. Everything on the far side of it was already committed to a detonation it didn't know about yet.

subject: cavern
fact: Behind me, deeper in the cavern, Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise.
source_quote: Behind me, deeper in the cavern, Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise.

subject: cavern
fact: The cavern is the site of Asha Vandree’s long-standing isolation, where she waits for a solution to walk through the door and where Ilvara’s fungal influence has taken root.
source_quote: she had been sitting in this cavern, waiting for a solution to walk through the door. We were, apparently, the solution.

subject: Cavern of the Heart Fungus
fact: A subterranean chamber dominated by the pulsing Heart Fungus, with elevated platforms, fungal growths, and a bridge over a pit smelling of decay. It is the site of Ilvara’s transformation and the battlefield for the entire engagement.
source_quote: She was on an elevated platform. Corrupted. The fungal growth had changed her in ways that were specific and terrible...

subject: Dust of Suleiman sphere radius
fact: The Dust of Suleiman creates a 20-foot sphere.
source_quote: it creates a 20-foot sphere

subject: fungal floor
fact: The fungal floor is a surface upon which the spider scurries back on cue, and where the Dancing Lights are woven around it with quiet precision.
source_quote: The spider scurried back across the fungal floor toward me on cue, and I was already weaving the lights around it — not frantically, not with the showy flick of wrists that amateur illusionists love, but with the quiet precision of someone who has thought this through to the fourth step.

subject: Glyph of Warding placement
fact: The Glyph of Warding is inscribed on the bridge and triggers when anyone approaches from Jorlan's side.
source_quote: And then, I guess the trigger is — anyone approaching from the side that Jorlan is on.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is the central mechanism of Ilvara's control over the cavern — it pulses, emits spores, and sustains her spore servants; its destruction dismantles her power architecture.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus was the key. That was her point, and she wasn't wrong.

subject: Heart Fungus position
fact: The Heart Fungus is the central mechanism of Ilvara's control over the entire area.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus was the key. That was her point, and she wasn't wrong. The fungus was how Ilvara kept control over the whole area.

subject: Ilvara's platform position
fact: Ilvara is on an elevated platform, preoccupied with the mushroom token, while the Heart Fungus pulses between her and the party.
source_quote: She was on an elevated platform. Corrupted. The fungal growth had changed her in ways that were specific and terrible... She was preoccupied with the mushroom token.

subject: shadow where Zalthir stood
fact: The shadow where Zalthir stood is a place of deliberate concealment, from which he observes Asha Vandree’s interactions with Daz without being acknowledged.
source_quote: I stepped out of the shadow where I had been standing.

subject: The Bridge
fact: The bridge is no longer a passage but a threshold of death — a line drawn by the glyph that separates those who are trusted from those who are not. It is a physical manifestation of the party’s moral compromise, where loyalty replaces judgment and direction replaces identity.
source_quote: The bridge was now a threshold. Everything on the far side of it was already committed to a detonation it didn't know about yet.

subject: The Cavern
fact: A subterranean chamber under Ilvara’s control, saturated with fungal growth, spore-laden air, and magical residue from the Heart Fungus. The cavern’s architecture is tied to the fungus’s power, and its hidden dangers include lingering markers from Gracklstugh’s pocket dimension that make certain individuals vulnerable to the artifact.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension, had left a marker on us. The mushroom artifact could exploit it.

subject: The Cavern of the Heart Fungus
fact: The Cavern of the Heart Fungus is a vast, oppressive Underdark chamber dominated by a massive pulsing fungal growth. The air is thick with spores, the ground is littered with the remnants of fallen drow, and the walls are stained with fungal veins. It is both a temple and a prison — Ilvara’s throne room and the source of her dominion.
source_quote: She was on an elevated platform. Corrupted. The fungal growth had changed her in ways that were specific and terrible.

subject: the fungal cavern
fact: The fungal cavern is a subterranean environment saturated with sentient spores, where natural features are indistinguishable from magical corruption, and where silence and stillness are critical to deception.
source_quote: "the fungal floor" ... "fungal shadows" ... "the Underdark"

subject: The Underdark Cavern
fact: A vast, fungal-laden cavern where Ilvara’s cult operates, saturated with spores, corrupted magic, and the lingering presence of Zuggtmoy. The floor is covered in fungal growth, shadows are thick, and inanimate objects (like Glabbagool) struggle to remain passive.
source_quote: The spider scurried back across the fungal floor toward me on cue... the dark of the Underdark with a gelatinous cube behind me failing to be a rock.

subject: Underdark
fact: The Underdark is the dark, subterranean realm where Daz stands with Glabbagool behind him failing to be a rock, and where Asha Vandree’s paranoia thrives.
source_quote: I stood in the dark of the Underdark with a gelatinous cube behind me failing to be a rock, and I considered the specific difficulty of selling a lie to someone whose paranoia keeps generating better explanations than the truth.

subject: Velkynvelve elevation
fact: Velkynvelve sits 100 feet above the cavern floor.
source_quote: Drow outpost was 100' in the sky

subject: Whorlstone Caverns
fact: The Whorlstone Caverns are the pocket dimension visited earlier, where a marker was left on the party — later exploited by the mushroom artifact as a vulnerability.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension, had left a marker on us.

subject: zone of Darkness
fact: A zone of Darkness is placed behind the party’s position as a fallback, not at the entrance, to provide concealment if the line breaks during the assault on Ilvara.
source_quote: I placed a zone of Darkness behind our position — not at the entrance, not anywhere Ilvara might notice the edge of it and understand what was coming. Behind us. A fallback. A place to pull someone if the line broke.

subject: zone of Darkness placement
fact: A zone of Darkness was placed behind the party's position as a fallback.
source_quote: I placed a zone of Darkness behind our position

subject: chasme count
fact: Four chasme demons are present in the cavern above the prisoners' tower.
source_quote: four chasme and two vrock

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: A magical substance used to burn the Heart Fungus, disrupting its control mechanism. It is not a creature but a targeted tactical tool deployed to neutralize the core of the enemy’s power.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman burns the Heart Fungus.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze familiar capable of forming intentional shapes and utterances — an anomaly that defies its expected inanimate nature. It responds to Daz’s commands with uncanny precision, suggesting a level of sentience or bond that exceeds typical magical familiars. Its behavior is interpreted by Asha as eccentricity, but its capacity for communication marks it as a dangerous and unusual entity.
source_quote: Glabbagool, I'm taking care of this, it's fine.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze that was introduced as Daz’s familiar — its blinking eyes and unnatural presence were disguised to avoid panic, and its status as a familiar granted it unexpected respect from Asha.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a colossal, pulsing fungal entity that serves as the architectural core of Ilvara’s control over the cavern. It emits lethal spore clouds, reacts to intruders, and is the true source of her power — not Ilvara herself. Destroying it dismantles her dominion.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus was the key. That was her point, and she wasn't wrong.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a powerful, possibly sentient fungal artifact tied to Ilvara’s operation. Though not the vector of infection, it is a dangerous focus of magical energy and must be destroyed to prevent residual corruption from persisting after Ilvara’s death.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus itself wasn't the vector. The spores were Ilvara's. The artifact was the other risk.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is being ground by Grygum and shudders as it delivers twenty force damage per turn.
source_quote: Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down... The thing shudders. Good. Let it shudder.

subject: Ilvara
fact: A high priestess and leader of the Heart Fungus cult, Ilvara wields control over the cavern through the fungus and its spores. She is not the source of infection but its conduit. Her death is secondary to the destruction of the Heart Fungus, which sustains her power. She is a tactical target, not a strategic one.
source_quote: Ilvara dies, the mushroom artifact is destroyed, the infection does not leave this cavern.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a known trickster entity associated with deception and illusions in the fungal Underdark, suspected by Asha of orchestrating false visions of Lolth's presence.
source_quote: "Is this another trick of Ilvara's?"

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Four former Velkynvelve guards reanimated by the Heart Fungus, shambling and corrupted. They emerge from the ground and contribute to battlefield congestion. They are vulnerable to area damage and glyph detonations.
source_quote: Then the spore servants come up out of the ground — four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong...

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Spore Servants are former drow guards and allies who have been fully consumed by Ilvara’s spores. They are shambling, broken, and mentally hollowed, yet retain enough physical coordination to fight. They are not undead or outsiders — they are people who chose ecstasy over autonomy.
source_quote: Four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong.

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Spore Servants are former drow who succumbed to Ilvara’s spores, embracing her claims of Lolth’s manifestation — they are not monsters, but hollowed-out people who made a choice.
source_quote: They are the drow of our party whom have totally succumbed to Ilvara's power... People. Hollowed out. Not monsters dragged in from somewhere else, but people who had made a choice.

subject: Spore Servants
fact: Spore servants are former drow who have been fully consumed by Ilvara’s spores, losing their autonomy and becoming mindless, ecstatic vessels. They are not external threats but internal tragedies — people who chose ecstasy over identity. The glyph will kill them indiscriminately, making them morally indistinct from innocent drow.
source_quote: People. Hollowed out. Not monsters dragged in from somewhere else, but people who had made a choice — a terrible choice, maybe a seduced choice — and were now walking around as the consequence of it.

subject: spore walker
fact: A spore walker climbs up behind Thorin and swings into nothing — the first attack misses clean, but the second connects for five damage.
source_quote: Then a spore walker climbs up behind me... the first swing misses clean — the thing reaches up and just swings into nothing... but the second one connects. Five damage.

subject: spore walker attack damage
fact: The spore walker's second swing deals five damage.
source_quote: Five damage

subject: the fungal spores
fact: The fungal spores are a source of madness in the Underdark, capable of infecting minds and causing delusions of divine possession — specifically linked to Zuggtmoy's influence and the false belief in the Bride's power.
source_quote: "have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power? Is this another trick of Ilvara's?"

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy is a fungal god whose influence manifests as madness, compelling those infected to believe they are conduits of divine power — a delusion Asha suspects has overtaken the wizard and Glabbagool.
source_quote: "possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power?"

subject: Zuggtmoy's Spores
fact: Zuggtmoy’s spores are a sentient, corrupting fungal influence that infects minds and bodies, inducing madness, false divine visions, and irreversible transformation into fungal horrors. They are the true vector of infection — not the Heart Fungus itself.
source_quote: Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power?

subject: Asha
fact: Asha is a drow who claims to have resisted Ilvara’s spores through devotion to Lolth, but her statements are undermined by her use of 'I believe' — indicating uncertainty rather than knowledge. She refuses to speak directly to the narrator, yet reveals deep personal history and emotional exhaustion over the Jorlan-Ilvara breakup. She is impressed by Daz’s ooze familiar and displays rare warmth when discussing interpersonal drama.
source_quote: I believe. ... The only three people who are no longer captured by her spores are myself and Jorlan... Do you have any idea how aggravating that is?

subject: Asha
fact: Asha is a strategic voice who prioritized infrastructure over emotional satisfaction, advocating for targeting the Heart Fungus over exploiting Ilvara’s psychological vulnerabilities.
source_quote: because Asha was right and the infrastructure was more important than the satisfying image of Ilvara's nightmares eating her alive.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree believes in the foulness of Ilvara and desires her death with theological fervor.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless. We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave! I fear that her disease will spread.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree believes the Heart Fungus is the key to Ilvara's control, and that infrastructure demolition is more valuable than direct attacks on Ilvara.
source_quote: That's an obvious one — use it on the big heart fungus.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree considers Daz more impressive after learning he has an ooze familiar, shifting her perception of him.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect. I could tell that she's now even more impressed with Daz, for securing the services of an ooze familiar.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree has rejected Ilvara’s bride heresy and clings to Lolth’s faith as her reason for remaining uninfected.
source_quote: Me, because I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth, and have rejected all of these claims of the bride heresy.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree holds deep disdain for the party, especially the speaker, and refuses to speak to them directly.
source_quote: She was, apparently, briefly impressed. 'Well put, well put,' she said. 'This was just a test. Don't touch me.'

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a contemptuous drow priestess who rejects Ilvara's bride heresy, clings to Lolth's faith, and holds deep personal disdain for Jorlan due to their past romantic entanglement with Ilvara. She believes — but does not know — the Heart Fungus is the key to Ilvara's power, and she refuses to speak directly to the narrator after losing respect for them.
source_quote: I believe. The particular spore illness only originates from Ilvara's spores and from her mushroom.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a fanatically devoted follower of Lolth who has been psychologically warped by prolonged exposure to fungal corruption and Ilvara’s influence. Her paranoia has become a self-reinforcing belief system that transforms deception into divine tests and infection into heresy.
source_quote: You are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a paranoid devotee of Lolth who interprets Daz’s deception as a divine test of her discernment, believing she has passed it.
source_quote: you are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth, who are willing to believe every charlatan magic user that is somehow being possessed by the power of Lolth.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a paranoid devotee who, after initially interpreting Daz’s con as divine deception, reframes it as a test of her discernment and believes she has passed it.
source_quote: you are trying to test me, to see if I was one of those fake followers of Lolth… I believe she had now passed.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is a surface-trained drow who has been deeply exposed to Zuggtmoy’s spore influence, exhibits extreme paranoia about contamination, and holds absolute theological conviction in Lolth’s will being perverted by Ilvara’s marriage cult. She is desperate, calculating, and relies on others to act where she cannot, while projecting authority over Daz as her designated agent. Her fear of direct contact with fungal corruption is visceral and earned.
source_quote: Don't touch me.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is referenced as the authority who decides the fate of failed Drow, and her point is that the Heart Fungus is the infrastructure of Ilvara's power — kill it to dismantle her control, not target her directly.
source_quote: Asha Vandree's territory, and I knew it.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree is watching with fractured eyes, interpreting every supernatural event as a test of her discernment, and has reframed the wizard's performance as divine validation of her own faithfulness to Lolth — then later as possible fungal possession by Zuggtmoy or trickery by Ilvara.
source_quote: "You're a wizard... a wizard who prays to Lolth?" ... "you are trying to test me..." ... "have you two been infected by the spores...?"

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree knows the Heart Fungus does not cause fungal disease beyond poisoning, pain, and breathing difficulties, but only believes the spore illness originates from Ilvara’s spores.
source_quote: The particular spore illness only originates from Ilvara's spores and from her mushroom. I believe.

subject: Asha Vandree
fact: Asha Vandree, a contemptuous drow priestess, possesses deep knowledge of the cavern's power structures and has corrected Grygum’s tactical focus, insisting that the Heart Fungus — not Ilvara — must be destroyed first to dismantle Ilvara’s control. She is reluctant to engage but provides critical insight, revealing that Grygum and Thorin carry a marker from Gracklstugh that makes them vulnerable to the artifact.
source_quote: I thought you had strong allies, who had a tactical awareness and understanding how to use their magic for destructive purposes.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer catches ambient light and turns it into something brighter, defying the darkness of the Underdark.
source_quote: The blade catches some ambient light from somewhere and turns it into something brighter, something that has no business existing this deep underground.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is Thorin’s sword, which he wields with precision and skill in melee combat against Jorlan.
source_quote: Now I have Dawnbringer in hand — the real hand, the right hand, the one that knows what it's doing...

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is still in my hand.
source_quote: Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Daz
fact: A member of the team who is attentive to Grygum’s spell explanations and expresses interest in Phantasmal Killer, indicating a tactical curiosity but no direct leadership role. His engagement suggests he may be a potential ally in executing the final plan.
source_quote: What's that?" Daz said. "Sounds fantastic.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a confident, improvisational agent who operates in the register of boldness indistinguishable from foolishness until it succeeds. He manipulates Asha’s theological framing by mirroring her language with plausible doubt, feigning sincerity to gain trust, and deftly redirects her expectations onto the party. He does not panic under pressure, and his tempo and presence convince Asha he is a true follower of Lolth — despite evidence suggesting otherwise.
source_quote: I already feel the gratitude of Lolth. I have that.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a frontline coordinator who analyzes spell depletion and brawler engagement windows. He advocates for timing the entry of melee units and supports team synergy through phase-based planning.
source_quote: Daz talked through the phases — the opening volley, the depletion of spell slots, the point at which the brawlers would need to go in.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a performer who has assumed the identity of a wizard communing with Lolth, using illusion, familiar manipulation, and psychological misdirection to convince Asha Vandree of divine possession. He is calm, calculated, and adept at reframing suspicion into belief.
source_quote: I am… you are not speaking to the wizard of this body. I… he… this body has communed with Lolth. And I… I am speaking through this body.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a pragmatic and emotionally intelligent member of the party who has been infected by Ilvara’s spores but retains his agency. He is the reluctant familiar-bearer of Glabbagool and serves as a bridge between Asha and the rest of the group, earning her begrudging respect through tact and insight.
source_quote: Our caution came from unfamiliarity with mushroom-related side effects, and that asking for expert guidance was tactically sound rather than ignorant.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is a wizard who has communed with Lolth and speaks through this body, using the spider and Dancing Lights as observable proof of his connection.
source_quote: I am… you are not speaking to the wizard of this body. I… he… this body has communed with Lolth. And I… I am speaking through this body.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is infected by Ilvara’s spores but maintains clarity, explaining caution as stemming from unfamiliarity with mushroom-related side effects. He is regarded with growing respect by Asha after being introduced as the owner of Glabbagool, an ooze familiar — a status that elevates his perceived power despite his condition.
source_quote: Explaining that our caution came from unfamiliarity with mushroom-related side effects, and that asking for expert guidance was tactically sound rather than ignorant.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is infected by spores — visibly altered — and serves as a visual warning to the party.
source_quote: I mean, — look at him! He's already infected.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is infected by spores — visibly altered — and serves as the visual proof that the spore threat is real and not theoretical, convincing the party to take precautions.
source_quote: I mean, — look at him! He's already infected. I don't want to be infected.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz is the only one Asha respects enough to speak to directly after the speaker loses her favor.
source_quote: My dear boy," she said, and then looked at me with contempt, and then turned to Daz.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.
source_quote: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, 24 damage worth of fire finding her even through her save, and the icon smolders.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz opens up with a Fireball shaped so precisely around his allies that it catches Ilvara and her precious mushroom icon in the center of it, dealing 24 damage worth of fire even through her save, and the icon smolders.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: Daz
fact: Daz smooths over tension by framing caution as tactical wisdom, earns Asha’s brief respect, and becomes the vessel through whom Asha communicates intelligence — the only one she speaks to directly after losing faith in the narrator.
source_quote: Well put, well put," she said. "This was just a test. Don't touch me.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube acting as a familiar, but he is incapable of maintaining silence or stillness. His attempts to be an inanimate object repeatedly fail due to his tendency to speak, move, and express agency — a persistent, comedic liability in high-stakes deception.
source_quote: I heard the reminder that invisible rocks do not speak. I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes, which then began tracking left and right with the particular energy of someone who absolutely cannot help himself.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube failing to remain motionless and silent as instructed; he has begun talking, moving his eyes, and narrating his own invisibility, despite being told to be a feature of the cavern.
source_quote: "Glabbagool," I said... "I'm taking care of this. It's fine." ... "he started *talking*. I heard the reminder that invisible rocks do not speak. I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes..."

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is a gelatinous cube familiar that fails to remain inert, speaking and moving despite being instructed to be a silent feature of the cavern.
source_quote: he started *talking*. I heard the reminder that invisible rocks do not speak. I heard — I am fairly certain I heard — the small wet sound of him opening his eyes, which then began tracking left and right with the particular energy of someone who absolutely cannot help himself.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze creature mistaken for a familiar by the party to conceal its true nature. It blinks passively, seemingly indifferent to being mislabeled, yet its presence forces the group to confront the absurdity of categorization in the face of existential horror. It deserves recognition for enduring the indignity.
source_quote: Glabbagool blinked. Probably didn't mind.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze creature mistaken for a familiar by the party to explain his presence, and he does not seem to mind the misclassification.
source_quote: Thorin introduced Glabbagool as Daz's familiar. Glabbagool blinked. Probably didn't mind.

subject: Glabbagool
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze entity mistaken for a familiar by the party to conceal its true nature. It blinks passively, seemingly indifferent to being mislabeled, yet its presence as an ooze familiar impresses Asha and adds an element of tactical misdirection.
source_quote: An ooze familiar," she said, looking at Daz now with something approaching respect.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum believes Phantasmal Killer is a just spell because it taps into a creature's deepest fears.
source_quote: A spell that reaches into something's mind and pulls out what it's afraid of. Bahamut didn't teach me that one, exactly, but I don't think he'd object. Some fears are just.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a spellcaster carrying three potent 4th-level spells — Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, and Phantasmal Killer — but limited to casting only one due to a single spell slot. He is methodical, strategic, and burdened by the weight of choosing which tool will define the mission’s outcome.
source_quote: Three keys. One lock. The planning was, in a sense, just a very elaborate way of deciding which door we most needed to open.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a spellcaster who lays out three 4th-level spells — Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, and Phantasmal Killer — but can only cast one due to having only one 4th-level spell slot.
source_quote: So these powerful spells I've been talking about… they're all 4th level, and I only have one fourth level slot. I can only cast one.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise.
source_quote: Behind me, deeper in the cavern, Grygum is grinding the Heart Fungus down with something that sounds like the word *Suleiman* and delivers twenty force damage per turn like a promise.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is planning the assassination of Ilvara, having evaluated three 4th-level spells — Glyph of Warding, Dust of Suleiman, and Phantasmal Killer — and realizing he can only cast one due to limited spell slots. He is seeking tactical input from Asha Vandree and has internalized her correction that the Heart Fungus, not Ilvara, is the true target.
source_quote: It's a… the spell is Glyph of Warding," I said, because someone had asked and I'd been waiting for the right moment to explain it. "You inscribe it in a particular place, and then when somebody triggers it by moving across it, it does its thing."

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is the planner who placed the Glyph of Warding on the bridge with deliberate patience, creating a hidden tactical asset later exploited by Thorin.
source_quote: He's also standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a corrupted former guardian now fused with the Heart Fungus, wielding a scourge and preoccupied with a mushroom token. She is reconfiguring the battle in real time, and her transformation is both specific and terrible.
source_quote: She was on an elevated platform. Corrupted. The fungal growth had changed her in ways that were specific and terrible — the scourge still in her hand, but everything else altered.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is a former high priestess of Lolth who has been seduced by the idea that Lolth wishes to be married, and now spreads fungal corruption through her spores.
source_quote: Ilvara, who was once a high priestess of Lolth, has become seduced by this abomination, this idea that Lolth wishes to be married. There is something foul and stinking about her, and then all of those allies she seems to covet have turned into fungal creatures that are mindless.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is bleeding after being caught in Daz's Fireball, which struck her precious mushroom icon with 24 damage despite her save, and the icon now smolders.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is bleeding, her mushroom icon is smoldering, and the math has changed.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is bleeding.
source_quote: Ilvara is bleeding.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is corrupted by fungal growth, preoccupied with the mushroom token, and has transformed into a being whose control is tied to the Heart Fungus.
source_quote: She was on an elevated platform. Corrupted. The fungal growth had changed her in ways that were specific and terrible — the scourge still in her hand, but everything else altered.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is corrupted by fungal growth, retains the scourge in her hand, and uses the Heart Fungus to control spore servants — her power is not merely personal but systemic.
source_quote: She was on an elevated platform. Corrupted. The fungal growth had changed her in ways that were specific and terrible — the scourge still in her hand, but everything else altered.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara is the source of the spore illness and the one who seduced drow into embracing the ecstasy of the spores.
source_quote: who embraced the spores and the ecstasy that came through them.

subject: Ilvara
fact: Ilvara was once romantically involved with Jorlan, and their breakup left him bitter and broken.
source_quote: They used to have an affair... and then she broke up with him, and then he was bitter because she broke up with him.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a bitter drow who was abandoned by Ilvara after an affair, now nursing a wounded pride and consumed by resentment. He is not captured by her spores, stands outside the party’s trust, and is unknowingly manipulated into triggering the Glyph of Warding on the bridge.
source_quote: Jorlan still is complaining that Ilvara… Ilvara this and Ilvara that.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a bitter former lover of Ilvara, abandoned and enraged — his predictable rage was weaponized by Thorin to trigger the Glyph of Warding, turning his emotional wound into tactical leverage.
source_quote: Jorlan is across the cavern, bitter-eyed, nursing whatever wound his pride has taken since Ilvara discarded him.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a drow who rejected Ilvara’s spores not through devotion but out of personal bitterness over a broken romantic relationship with her. He is distrusted by the party, positioned as the trigger side of the glyph, and remains emotionally fixated on Ilvara despite the chaos of the Abyss.
source_quote: Jorlan still is complaining that Ilvara… Ilvara this and Ilvara that.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is a humiliated ex-ally of Ilvara, emotionally broken and standing directly on a Glyph of Warding. His rage is predictable, his vector clear — exploited by Thorin as a tactical weapon.
source_quote: He's across the cavern, bitter-eyed, nursing whatever wound his pride has taken since Ilvara discarded him.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is bitter, enraged, and emotionally wounded by Ilvara’s rejection, making him a predictable target.
source_quote: Jorlan... bitter-eyed, nursing whatever wound his pride has taken since Ilvara discarded him.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is still in front of me.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Jorlan
fact: Jorlan is still in front of the attacker, staggered but not broken, still angry, and the fight is not over.
source_quote: Jorlan staggers. He doesn't fall.

subject: Lolth
fact: Lolth is invoked by Asha as the source of her faith — the only reason she resists Ilvara’s spores — and is contrasted with Ilvara’s heretical claim that the bride is Lolth’s further manifestation.
source_quote: I have diligently kept the faith to Lolth, and have rejected all of these claims of the bride heresy.

subject: Lolth
fact: Lolth is the Spider Queen, worshipped by Asha Vandree as an absolute deity whose will is cold and unyielding, and whose claimed gratitude Daz asserts he already possesses.
source_quote: The gratitude of Lolth… I already feel the gratitude of Lolth… That is not the kind of conviction a follower of Lolth shows.

subject: The Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is most valuable as infrastructure demolition, not as a direct weapon against Ilvara.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman, which I had been imagining pouring down on Ilvara directly, was actually more valuable as infrastructure demolition.

subject: The Speaker
fact: The speaker takes emotional notes on Asha Vandree, seeing her as more human than they initially believed, despite her hostility.
source_quote: I took notes. Not on the tactics — on Asha, who was more person than I'd given her credit for, even if she refused to speak to me directly.

subject: The Spore Servants
fact: The Spore Servants are former drow who have been hollowed out by Ilvara’s spores and now serve as shambling, corrupted enforcers.
source_quote: four of them, former Velkynvelve guards, shambling and wrong

subject: the wizard (narrator)
fact: The wizard has performed an elaborate illusion using a spider, Dancing Lights, and vocal persona to impersonate a vessel of Lolth — a con that was not seen through, but instead reinterpreted by Asha as a divine test and then as fungal infection.
source_quote: "I am… you are not speaking to the wizard of this body. I… he… this body has communed with Lolth. And I… I am speaking through this body." ... "There are many imitations... I came to you in my smaller form, and led you here."

subject: Thorin
fact: A team member who, along with Grygum, visited the site of Ilvara’s operation and now carries the Gracklstugh marker. He is identified as unsuitable to handle the artifact directly due to this vulnerability, though his specific role in the assassination remains undefined.
source_quote: I think they were the two that went to visit, what's her name, right? — yeah, you two probably don't want to be near it, but everybody else is fine.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf brawler who accepts his role as a close-quarters combatant despite lacking ranged options. He adapts by accepting a crossbow, manipulates battlefield terrain and enemy psychology to trigger the Glyph of Warding against Jorlan, and fights with brutal pragmatism once engaged.
source_quote: Come get it, idiot!

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf brawler who accepts ranged roles out of necessity, wields a crossbow reluctantly, and holds the line with Dawnbringer when forced into melee. He respects tactical leverage and operates on terrain-based intuition learned from giants.
source_quote: I know this. I made peace with it before the fight started. Mostly.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf brawler who adapts to ranged combat with borrowed gear, uses terrain and psychology to manipulate Jorlan into triggering the glyph, and fights with Dawnbringer once engaged.
source_quote: I put the crossbow down... I just have to give him a target.

subject: Thorin, son of the Ember Vanguard
fact: Thorin is flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse while the fight rages in all directions around him.
source_quote: A spore walker climbs up behind me... Thorin, son of the Ember Vanguard, flanked by a dead man's fungal corpse while the fight rages in all directions around him.

subject: Zalthir
fact: A thoughtful team member who raises the critical issue of spore containment after the Heart Fungus is destroyed. His concern indicates awareness of the broader ecological and strategic implications of the mission beyond immediate combat.
source_quote: Zalthir, bless him, raised the broader concern about spores. He'd been thinking about it — we all had.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a cautious, anxious spellcaster who obsesses over spore infections and mushroom-related dangers, having witnessed their effects firsthand on Daz. He devises the critical tactical maneuver to grapple Ilvara and drop her into the Phantasmal Killer, demonstrating strategic depth despite his fears.
source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them, and then the rest of you can fireball or whatever from there.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a drow operative trained in social erasure and silent observation. He is acutely aware of being ignored by Asha Vandree and uses this marginalization as tactical intelligence, cataloging every detail of the negotiation without drawing attention to himself.
source_quote: She filed me away and returned her eyes to Daz. Not a glance afterward. Not a word in my direction for the duration of the conversation.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a drow who observes Asha Vandree’s refusal to acknowledge him, treated as equipment rather than a person during negotiations.
source_quote: She filed me away and returned her eyes to Daz. Not a glance afterward. Not a word in my direction for the duration of the conversation.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a teleporting tactician who executes high-risk grapple-and-drop maneuvers. He targets the Heart Fungus as the central mechanism of control and coordinates team damage to maximize overlap.
source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them, and then the rest of you can fireball or whatever from there.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is deeply concerned about spore infection and believes the party’s caution is justified.
source_quote: You worry about these things a lot. Yes," Zalthir said. "We do, yeah," I agreed.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir raises concerns about spores, suggests teleporting Ilvara into the Phantasmal Killer, and demonstrates tactical awareness — he is the architect of the final kill sequence.
source_quote: I can try to grab Ilvara and drop her into that, such that you're hurting both of them, and then the rest of you can fireball or whatever from there.

subject: Zuggtmoy
fact: Zuggtmoy is a fungal god whose spores are suspected by Asha Vandree of infecting Daz and Glabbagool, leading her to question whether their actions are deception, divinity, or madness.
source_quote: have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy? convinced of the bride's power?

subject: Dancing Lights
fact: Dancing Lights are shaped not into floating globes but into a towering, feminine silhouette of eight eyes and infinite patience, used by Daz to simulate the presence of the Spider Queen.
source_quote: Dancing Lights, shaped not into floating globes but into something grander — a silhouette, towering and feminine and terrible, the suggestion of eight eyes and infinite patience.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is still in my hand.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Dawnbringer is still in the attacker's hand as the confrontation continues.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Dawnbringer
fact: Thorin’s ancestral sword, a weapon of radiant light that defies the darkness of the cavern. It is his primary melee tool, wielded with precision after accepting a crossbow as a placeholder.
source_quote: Now I have Dawnbringer in hand — the real hand, the right hand, the one that knows what it's doing...

subject: Daz's role as healer
fact: Daz rationalizes the party's caution as tactical wisdom rather than ignorance, earning Asha's brief approval.
source_quote: Daz smoothed it over, as Daz does — explaining that our caution came from unfamiliarity with mushroom-related side effects, and that asking for expert guidance was tactically sound rather than ignorant.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: A 4th-level evocation spell capable of creating a 20-foot sphere of damaging dust at 120-foot range, dealing 20 points of damage per turn to all within. Originally intended for direct use on Ilvara, it is now repositioned as a tool for destroying the Heart Fungus and its supporting infrastructure.
source_quote: So I also have another spell I haven't had a chance to use yet called the Dust of Suleiman... It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: A 4th-level spell that creates a 20-foot sphere of destructive energy, dealing 20 points of damage per turn to all creatures within. It is a long-range area denial tool, ideal for clearing groups or creating chokepoints in confined spaces.
source_quote: It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: Dust of Suleiman is a spell that creates a 20-foot sphere at 120-foot range, dealing 20 points of damage per turn to anything inside it, used by Grygum in the assassination plan.
source_quote: I also have another spell I haven't had a chance to use yet called the Dust of Suleiman… It creates a 20-foot sphere, and anything inside this sphere takes 20 points of damage per turn.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is a powerful magical substance initially intended for direct use against Ilvara, but correctly identified by Asha as more effective as an infrastructure weapon — capable of destroying the Heart Fungus and severing Ilvara’s control over the area.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman, which I had been imagining pouring down on Ilvara directly, was actually more valuable as infrastructure demolition.

subject: Dust of Suleiman
fact: The Dust of Suleiman was imagined as a direct weapon against Ilvara, but proved more valuable as an infrastructure-demolition tool — its true use is against the Heart Fungus, not the person.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman, which I had been imagining pouring down on Ilvara directly, was actually more valuable as infrastructure demolition.

subject: Dust of Suleiman damage
fact: The Dust of Suleiman deals 20 points of damage per turn.
source_quote: takes 20 points of damage per turn

subject: Dust of Suleiman range
fact: The Dust of Suleiman can be cast at a 120-foot distance.
source_quote: I can cast at a 120-foot distance

subject: Dust of Suleiman use
fact: The Dust of Suleiman is more valuable as infrastructure demolition than as a direct weapon against Ilvara.
source_quote: The Dust of Suleiman, which I had been imagining pouring down on Ilvara directly, was actually more valuable as infrastructure demolition.

subject: Glabbagool identity
fact: Glabbagool is an ooze that was falsely introduced as Daz's familiar to conceal its true nature.
source_quote: Thorin solved it with characteristic practicality. 'Will Glabbagool be offended if we refer to him as a familiar? I think that's probably the easiest way to just explain it away,' he muttered. Then the dwarf introduced Glabbagool as Daz's familiar.

subject: Glyph of the Bridge
fact: The glyph inscribed on the bridge is a lethal trap designed to detonate upon approach from Jorlan’s side. It is a blunt instrument with no capacity for judgment — it kills based on direction, not intent, morality, or affiliation. Its design reflects the party’s moral compromise: they chose to kill those they distrust, not those who are truly evil.
source_quote: I don't know how to inscribe a glyph that will only kill the drow that we don't like. ... The glyph doesn't have opinions. It just detonates.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: A 4th-level enchantment spell that inscribes a magical trap on a surface or object, triggering when a creature interacts with it. It can be configured to deal damage, release a spell, or activate a condition. It is ideal for ambushes, chokepoints, or silent eliminations.
source_quote: You inscribe it in a particular place, and then when somebody triggers it by moving across it, it does its thing.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: A strategically placed magical trap on the bridge, set by Grygum, designed to detonate when triggered. It is exploited by Thorin as a force multiplier against Jorlan’s charge.
source_quote: He's also standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding that Grygum spent real patience setting into the stone of the bridge.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: Glyph of Warding is a spell inscribed in a specific location to trigger upon movement across it, used by Grygum as part of the assassination plan against Ilvara.
source_quote: It's a… the spell is Glyph of Warding… You inscribe it in a particular place, and then when somebody triggers it by moving across it, it does its thing.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding is a magical trap inscribed on the bridge by Grygum, designed to detonate upon approach from Jorlan’s side. It is used not as a defensive measure, but as a tactical lure, exploiting Jorlan’s rage to eliminate both him and nearby spore servants in a single burst.
source_quote: Jorlan… standing exactly twenty feet from the Glyph of Warding... I put the crossbow down.

subject: Glyph of Warding
fact: The Glyph of Warding was inscribed on the bridge to detonate against anyone approaching from Jorlan’s side — it does not distinguish friend from foe, only direction, making it a blunt instrument of tactical exclusion.
source_quote: The glyph went down on the bridge... I don't know how to inscribe a glyph that will only kill the drow that we don't like.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: A massive, sentient fungal entity serving as the central power source and control mechanism for Ilvara’s operation. It is not the vector of infection — its spores are — but its destruction will collapse Ilvara’s authority over the cavern. It is the true target of the assassination plan.
source_quote: The Heart Fungus itself wasn't the vector. The spores were Ilvara's.

subject: Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is a mushroom artifact that is not the vector of infection, but remains a secondary risk alongside Ilvara’s spores.
source_quote: the Heart Fungus itself wasn't the vector. The spores were Ilvara's. The artifact was the other risk.

subject: Light Crossbow
fact: The light crossbow was lent by the narrator to Thorin, enabling his contribution to the ranged phase of the battle — a small act of tactical inclusion that restored his role in the fight.
source_quote: I can lend — I can lend you my light crossbow.

subject: light crossbow transfer
fact: The light crossbow is lent to Thorin to compensate for his lack of ranged capability.
source_quote: I can lend — I can lend you my light crossbow.

subject: Mushroom Artifact
fact: A mysterious fungal artifact, likely tied to Ilvara’s cult and Zuggtmoy’s influence, serves as the source or amplifier of the spore-based corruption. Its nature is not directly described, but its effects — mindless fungal allies, theological delusion, and contagious transformation — are central to Asha’s motivation and the party’s mission. It is the target of the planned eradication.
source_quote: We need to kill her. We need to butcher her! We need to send her to an unearthly grave!

subject: Mushroom Artifact
fact: The mushroom artifact left a marker on the party from the Whorlstone Caverns — it can exploit that marker, making the party vulnerable to its influence unless they act deliberately.
source_quote: The mushroom artifact could exploit it.

subject: mushroom icon
fact: The mushroom icon is smoldering after being struck by Daz's Fireball with 24 damage, despite Ilvara's save.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: mushroom icon
fact: The mushroom icon is smoldering after taking 24 fire damage from Daz's Fireball.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning... the icon smolders.

subject: mushroom icon
fact: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: Phantasmal Killer
fact: A 4th-level illusion spell that taps into a creature’s deepest fears, creating an illusory manifestation that causes psychic damage if the target fails successive Wisdom saving throws. It can kill in a minute if the target fails each turn’s save. Grygum considers it a potent psychological weapon but cannot cast it without sacrificing another spell.
source_quote: It says you tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see and create an illusory manifestation of its deepest fears. They become frightened if they fail a wisdom saving throw... then they take 4 die 10 psychic damage.

subject: Phantasmal Killer
fact: A 4th-level illusion spell that taps into a creature’s deepest fears, manifesting them as an illusory horror. If the target fails successive Wisdom saves, they take 4d10 psychic damage per turn for up to a minute. It is a psychological weapon designed to break the mind before the body.
source_quote: It says you tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see and create an illusory manifestation of its deepest fears.

subject: Phantasmal Killer
fact: Phantasmal Killer is a 4th-level spell that taps into a creature’s deepest fears, creating an illusory manifestation that can deal 4d10 psychic damage if the target fails consecutive Wisdom saving throws.
source_quote: Phantasmal Killer… it says you tap into the nightmares of a creature you can see and create an illusory manifestation of its deepest fears… they take 4 die 10 psychic damage.

subject: Phantasmal Killer damage
fact: Phantasmal Killer deals 4d10 psychic damage if the target fails saving throws each turn.
source_quote: takes 4 die 10 psychic damage

subject: Phantasmal Killer range
fact: Phantasmal Killer has a 120-foot range.
source_quote: 120-foot range

subject: Silence of deliberate erasure
fact: The silence of deliberate erasure is the drow societal weapon used by Asha Vandree to treat Zalthir as furniture, not a person, during negotiations.
source_quote: There is a particular kind of silence that drow society uses as a weapon. Not the comfortable silence of empty stone corridors… the silence of deliberate erasure. Of being present in a room and being treated as furniture.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The silver candlesticks flanking the Lolth altar are worth 25 gp each.
source_quote: a pair of heavy silver candlesticks worth 25 gp each

subject: Spider
fact: The Spider is a small, real creature, convincing enough if one does not look too closely at the absence of divine ichor, and serves as Daz’s familiar and tangible proof of his connection to Lolth.
source_quote: my familiar. A small spider, real enough, convincing enough if you don't look too hard at the absence of divine ichor.

subject: Spores
fact: The spores are Ilvara’s primary vector of infection, distinct from the Heart Fungus artifact, and feared by Asha Vandree as a contagious, mind-altering plague.
source_quote: The spores were Ilvara's. The artifact was the other risk.

subject: Zuggtmoy's Spores
fact: Zuggtmoy’s spores are a fungal contagion that induces madness, possession, and physical transformation. They are the vector of Ilvara’s cult’s expansion and the source of Asha’s paranoia. The spores are airborne, persistent, and capable of infecting even those who believe themselves immune. Their specific vectors and resistance patterns are the hidden intelligence Asha unknowingly revealed.
source_quote: Have you two been infected by the spores, possessed by the crazed magic of Zuggtmoy?

subject: Asha’s Fear of Contact
fact: Asha Vandree’s repeated aversion to physical proximity — culminating in 'Don't touch me' — reveals a deep, personal terror of fungal contamination. This fear is not abstract; it is embodied, earned through prolonged exposure to Zuggtmoy’s influence. It explains her reliance on others and her refusal to act directly against Ilvara, making her a key source of intelligence despite her hostility.
source_quote: Don't touch me.

subject: Asha’s Refusal to Speak
fact: Asha refuses to speak directly to the narrator after losing respect for them, delivering all critical intelligence through Daz. This silent estrangement hints at deeper personal wounds and unresolved tension — a thread that may influence future alliances or betrayals.
source_quote: Tell the Dragonborn that... she looked at me with contempt, and then turned to Daz.

subject: Asha’s Silence Toward the Narrator
fact: Asha refuses to speak directly to the narrator, signaling a broken trust. Yet she reveals more about herself in private monologues than she ever does in direct conversation — suggesting the narrator’s exclusion is not about information, but emotional distance.
source_quote: because I had apparently lost her respect at some point and she was going to make sure I knew it.

subject: Asha Vandree's belief
fact: Asha Vandree says 'I believe' about the origin of the spore illness, undermining her own authority and leaving the truth unverified.
source_quote: I believe.

subject: Asha Vandree's fear of contamination
fact: Asha Vandree fears fungal contamination personally and deeply, but the origin of this fear is not specified.
source_quote: Don't touch me.

subject: changed math
fact: The outcome of the encounter has shifted due to the Fireball's effect on Ilvara and her icon, altering the tactical balance.
source_quote: The mushroom is burning. Ilvara is bleeding. The math has changed.

subject: fight unresolved
fact: The confrontation remains unresolved — Jorlan is still angry, the Heart Fungus is active, Ilvara is wounded, and Dawnbringer is still drawn.
source_quote: Jorlan is still in front of me, and Dawnbringer is still in my hand.

subject: Glabbagool's failure
fact: Glabbagool’s inability to remain passive has disrupted the performance and introduced an unpredictable variable — his verbal outbursts and eye movements risk exposing the illusion to Asha or others.
source_quote: "he started *talking*. I heard the reminder that invisible rocks do not speak..."

subject: Glabbagool's nature
fact: Glabbagool is supposed to be an inanimate ooze familiar but speaks and moves, and his true nature is unexplained.
source_quote: The ooze had, apparently, opinions about the negotiation. It began to form the shape of an utterance — which is not something you want from what is supposed to be an inanimate ooze familiar.

subject: Jorlan and Asha's history
fact: Jorlan and Ilvara once had an affair, she broke up with him, and he has been bitter ever since — a personal history the session leaves unexplored.
source_quote: They used to have an affair, it used to be this whole thing, and then she broke up with him, and then he was bitter because she broke up with him.

subject: Jorlan's grievance
fact: Jorlan hates Ilvara for something or other, but the specific reason is unstated and unresolved.
source_quote: Jorlan, because apparently he really hates Ilvara for something or other.

subject: Marker from Gracklstugh
fact: A lingering magical signature acquired during a visit to a pocket dimension in Gracklstugh’s Whorlstone Caverns, which now makes Grygum and Thorin vulnerable to the Heart Fungus artifact. The marker’s nature and origin are unknown, but its presence dictates who can safely handle or approach the artifact.
source_quote: Whatever we'd picked up in Gracklstugh in the Whorlstone Caverns when we visited the pocket dimension, had left a marker on us. The mushroom artifact could exploit it.

subject: Phantasmal Killer Target
fact: The nature of Ilvara’s deepest fears — and what an illusory manifestation of them would look like — remains unknown. This is an unexploited tactical avenue, hinted at but not acted upon.
source_quote: Phantasmal Killer reaches into nightmares. What does she dream about? What would an illusory manifestation of her deepest fears look like?

subject: Spore Containment Strategy
fact: A lingering concern among the group — particularly Zalthir — about how to prevent the spores from escaping the cavern after the Heart Fungus is destroyed. No plan has yet been formalized, but the risk is acknowledged as critical to mission success.
source_quote: Zalthir, bless him, raised the broader concern about spores. He'd been thinking about it — we all had.

subject: Tactical Leverage Over Terrain
fact: Thorin’s entire approach is built on leveraging position, enemy psychology, and environmental hazards rather than raw power. This philosophy remains the unspoken core of his tactics.
source_quote: I have been thinking in terrain and leverage since before I could name those words for what they were.

subject: The Broken Heart in the Abyss
fact: The lingering romantic feud between Ilvara and Jorlan persists amid cosmic collapse, revealing the drow’s stubborn humanity. Their emotional entanglement undermines the party’s strategic clarity and forces moral reckoning — love outlasts even the end of the world.
source_quote: The world is ending and someone's still nursing a broken heart in the middle of it.

subject: The Corruption of Lolth's Worship
fact: The conflict between traditional Lolth worship and Ilvara’s fungal heresy exposes a schism in divine authority — is Lolth a spider goddess of domination, or a bride of fungus? The answer determines who is heretic and who is faithful.
source_quote: Ilvara’s idea that Lolth wishes to be married... We need to kill her. We need to butcher her!

subject: The Heart Fungus
fact: The Heart Fungus is mentioned as a risk, but its nature and location are not clarified.
source_quote: The artifact was the other risk. Contain both and the job was done.

subject: The Meaning of 'I Believe'
fact: Asha’s use of 'I believe' — rather than 'I know' — subtly unravels her authority and exposes the fragility of dogma in the face of trauma. The narrator stores this phrase as a warning: certainty is a lie, and belief is the first step toward corruption.
source_quote: I believe. Two words that undermined everything she'd just said with such authority.

subject: The Nature of Belief in the Underdark
fact: A recurring theme: in the Underdark, belief is not a passive state but an active, malleable force that can be manipulated, inverted, or weaponized. Truth is irrelevant if the story someone tells themselves is more compelling than reality.
source_quote: There are players who don't know they're at the table. There are players who think they're winning. And then there is Asha Vandree, who had somehow managed to be both at once.

subject: The Nature of the Spore Infection
fact: The spore infection does not merely corrupt — it seduces. Victims experience ecstasy before losing their will, making them unwilling participants in their own transformation. This raises ethical questions about the Glyph of Warding and whether those affected are truly enemies or victims.
source_quote: People. Hollowed out. Not monsters dragged in from somewhere else, but people who had made a choice.

subject: The Party as Solution
fact: Asha Vandree has been waiting in the cavern for someone capable of confronting Ilvara’s spore cult at close range. She perceives the party — particularly Daz — as the solution she has been anticipating. Her admission that 'that is what you… where you come in' confirms she lacks the means to act herself and has strategically recruited others to do what she cannot.
source_quote: I was not going to kill her. That is what you… where you come in.

subject: The Silence of Zalthir
fact: Zalthir’s quiet observation represents a deeper narrative thread: the cost of invisibility. His erasure by Asha is not just an insult — it is a tactical advantage he weaponizes, revealing how power can be wielded without being seen.
source_quote: I have noticed this before. I will notice it again. I noted it, set it aside, and watched.

subject: the true nature of the performance
fact: The wizard’s deception — intended as a con to gain trust through assumed divine authority — has been overwritten by Asha’s paranoid interpretations, creating an unstable narrative where the truth is now indistinguishable from her layered delusions.
source_quote: She had not seen through the deception. She had reframed it entirely... built her a completely different story in which she was the clever one... She was not calling me a liar. She was asking whether I was a victim.

subject: Zalthir's role
fact: Zalthir was present during the entire negotiation but never acknowledged by Asha Vandree, and his contribution remains unstated.
source_quote: She filed me away and returned her eyes to Daz. Not a glance afterward. Not a word in my direction for the duration of the conversation.
